evidence.text: Two bird's wings opposed; two people back-to-back
Pictograph of two wings facing opposite directions.
違也。从飛下翄，取其相背。凡非之屬皆从非。

Pictogram (象形) - two wings facing opposite directions. Originally, it represented wings; then, according to Xu Shen, its meaning changed into "leave; disobey" (違). Eventually, it was used perhaps as a phonetic loan to mean "not to be".
Unrelated to the Kangxi radical 韭.
非 (OC *pɯj) is the fusion of the negation particle 不 (OC *pɯ, *pɯʔ, *pɯ', “not”) and the copula 惟 (OC *ɢʷi, “to be”), attested in oracle bone inscriptions.

evidence.field: 形義通解; character forms; Middle Chinese reading
evidence.text: The database interprets the oracle bone and bronze graph as wings spread to either side; following Xu Shen and Lin Yiguang, it proposes ‘wings’ as the original sense and derives ‘turn against’ from the wings facing away from one another. It records oracle-bone 非 in 《合集》16927, ‘非𡆥(憂)’, as a negative meaning ‘without worry’, and also as a place name. For bronze inscriptions it gives 毛公鼎’s ‘余非’ as ‘my faults’ and 中山王方壺’s ‘寡人非之’ as ‘I judge it wrong’; Warring States bamboo slips use 非 as a negator. The same page records 非母, 微 rhyme, level tone, division III, 甫微切.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 非

evidence.text: The page lists two oracle-bone examples, 15 of 23 bronze examples, 28 bamboo/slip examples, and one Small Seal example. This documents the database’s graph inventory but does not by itself establish a complete sequence of graphic changes. The pictured forms were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 非

evidence.field: 說文解字·非; 說文解字注
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry says ‘違也。从飛下翄，取其相背’ (‘opposition; from the lower wings of 飛, taking their facing away from one another’). The Duan Yucai commentary argues that 非 means 背 (‘face away’) rather than 離 (‘separate’), glossing the old reading as 韋. This is a Han-era explanatory tradition and commentary, not independent proof of original referent or semantic chronology.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text and later commentary
evidence.title: 非 fēi — 汉典

evidence.text: Records Mandarin IPA fei˥, Tang reading *biəi, Japanese HI (on) and SORERU/ARAZU (kun), Korean PI/비, Vietnamese phi, Cantonese fei1, and Guangyun category 非母 微韻 平聲, 甫微切, third division, closed. It also lists older system labels for Huang Kan and Wang Li, but not a reconstruction for a proposed phonetic element; 非 is not analyzed as a component in the account here.
evidence.title: 非 fēi — 汉典

evidence.source: Rōmaji / 古漢語 phonology article hosted by kurs10026.sakura.ne.jp
evidence.field: 非 negation; proposed ‘不唯’ fusion; sound history
evidence.text: The article gives matching oracle-bone contexts where 唯 and 非 occur as contrasting positive and negative formulations (《合集》33694 and 28299), and cites classical parallels. It reports Gao Heng (1943) and Pulleyblank (1959:178–180) as proposing 非 to be a fusion of 不 and 唯/惟. The article discusses disagreement over the reconstruction of 唯 and whether a sound change could make the fusion plausible; it presents the fusion as a proposal rather than a settled conclusion. Its table gives several systems: 非 *pəj in Baxter–Sagart 2014 and *pɯl in Zhengzhang (2003); 不 *pə / *pɯ and 唯 *ɢʷij (with a possible earlier *ɢʷuj) in those respective frameworks. This is phonological and lexical analysis, not evidence that the graph 非 was formed from graph components 不 and 唯.
evidence.title: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1 (PDF)

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology
evidence.text: Pei-chuan Wei’s 2001 article concerns the disputed fusion analysis of 弗 and 勿 (not 非): its abstract says some scholars oppose that analysis, and argues for it using complementary distribution and textual evidence. This provides context that fusion analyses in early Chinese negation are debated, but it does not directly establish or refute the separate 不 + 惟 analysis of 非.
evidence.title: 「弗」、「勿」拼合說新証 / New Evidence for the Hypothesis of Fu, Wu as Fusion Words

evidence.field: Old Chinese and Middle Chinese reading; semantic senses
evidence.text: The inspected page gives Mandarin fēi; Middle Chinese Baxter pjɨj, with fanqie 甫微切; Old Chinese Baxter–Sagart *pəj and Zhengzhang *pɯl. It lists the negating/copular sense, opposition, wrong/incorrect, and reproach/blame. It reports same-series characters, but does not supply component-level attestations demonstrating that 非 itself was originally a phonetic component in its own graph. Its separate claim that 非 fuses 不 and 惟 is an etymological proposal, not established by the source’s pronunciation table.
evidence.title: 非 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Studies of Unearthed Documents and Ancient Chinese Characters; Wang Qingju
evidence.text: Wang argues that 非 and 北 were nearly homophonous in Old Chinese and that 非 split from 北 during the oracle-bone period. She reads the early forms as two people back-to-back, with short strokes added to distinguish the negative graph. She reports that extant oracle-bone examples of 非 include negation and a possible place name, and lists examples in 《合集》10977, 33147, 34707–34709, 24156, 33694, 33479, and 16927–16928. This is Wang’s analysis, not an uncontested account.
evidence.title: 王青菊：釋“非”

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Studies of Unearthed Documents and Ancient Chinese Characters; Wang Qingju
evidence.field: Shuowen interpretation and competing formation accounts
evidence.text: The article summarizes Xu Shen’s Han-era account: 非 means opposition, formed from the lower wings of 飛 to express facing away; it also notes that this was taken to imply an extension to negation. Wang disputes that interpretation, observing that the oracle-bone use she surveyed is already negative and arguing that 飛 is later attested as a graph. She proposes a relation to 北 instead. Neither interpretation establishes a certain graphic origin or a dated semantic path from a pictorial referent.
evidence.kind: scholarly discussion of historical dictionary and disputed etymology
evidence.title: 王青菊：釋“非”

evidence.source: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1
evidence.field: graphic history; 非 and 飛; early attestations
evidence.text: The inspected article questions whether 非 is derived from 飛’s lower wings and says the oracle-bone, bronze, and Warring States forms do not determine whether the graphs share an origin. It cites oracle-bone examples 《合集》33694 (“非若”), 28299 (“非水”), and 24266 (“非”), bronze examples from 中山王壺 and 班簋, and Warring States slip examples from 郭店《老子》甲8 and 睡虎地《秦律》195. It reports no standalone oracle-bone graph 飛, with 飛 as a graph appearing later in its cited Chu and Zeng slips. These are scholarly source reports; object images were not visually inspected.
evidence.title: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1 (PDF)

evidence.source: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1
evidence.text: The article describes 非 as a negative adverb and notes that oracle-bone positive clauses with 唯 contrast with negative clauses using 非. It gives parallel questions in 《合集》33694 and 28299. This supports an early negative use but does not date the first use absolutely or establish whether that use developed from a sense such as ‘oppose’ or ‘face away’.
evidence.kind: scholarly discussion of early lexical use
evidence.title: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1 (PDF)

These dictionary citations document reported later uses, but their order on the page is not a chronology of semantic development.

evidence.field: proposed 不 + 惟 fusion and pronunciation comparisons
evidence.text: The article treats the proposal that spoken 非 is a fusion of 不 and 惟 as a debated phonological analysis. It compares oracle-bone clauses using 非 and 唯 and discusses disagreement over reconstructions and sound change. It explicitly does not demonstrate that the graph 非 is made from the graphs 不 and 惟. Since this proposal depends on a spoken source phrase, it does not establish an original depicted object or the name of one.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

search_audit.query: Inspected CUHK 非 character entry for script inventory and reported form/sense evidence
search_audit.outcome: Opened the character page and inspected its form inventory, Shuowen text, proposed wing interpretation, and listed oracle-bone and later examples.

gaps: No glyph image was visually inspected. The script inventory and wing interpretation are source assertions, not direct visual observations in this research.

The CUHK database’s oracle-bone negative example and its interpretation as ‘without worry’ were recorded, but the underlying inscription image and full context were not independently checked. The database also reports a place-name use without a specific cited example in the inspected passage.

Earliest attested graph use and earliest attested negative use cannot be assigned a precise absolute date from the inspected pages; ‘oracle bone’ is the earliest script class given. The date and contextual dating of 《合集》16927 were not verified.

The proposed wings → facing away → opposition/wrong semantic path is the CUHK/Shuowen account. It does not establish that the negative particle arose chronologically after ‘wings’ or ‘opposition’; extant oracle-bone material already shows a negative use.

The proposed 不 + 惟 fusion is disputed and depends on matching source-word reconstructions and a proposed phonological history. The inspected article notes differing analyses of 惟 and possible sound changes; this research did not establish the fusion as fact. It concerns a spoken construction and does not show that the graph 非 is graphically composed of 不 and 惟.

Non-loan semantic links between ‘opposition’, ‘wrong’, and the negative/coplasal use are not fully established by dated evidence in the inspected sources. The character’s other possible early lexical uses remain underexplored.

No proposed phonetic component in 非’s own graphic formation was found in the inspected analyses. Accordingly no phonetic-component ancestry or component-level reconstruction comparison is asserted; there is no distinct origin_form classification to assign.

The direct Baxter–Sagart reconstruction PDF was inaccessible in the web tool. The accessible secondary Wiktionary compilation reports *pəj for 非 and *pɯl for Zhengzhang (2003), but it is not a substitute for inspection of the primary reconstruction list.

The two modern analyses conflict: Wang Qingju proposes that 非 split from 北, while the PDF author says the graph evidence cannot establish a 非–飛 origin relationship and does not independently verify Wang’s 北 analysis. The original referent therefore remains unresolved.

The corpus examples establish reported Shang oracle-bone negative uses and a possible place-name use, but this search did not verify absolute dates for individual inscriptions or inspect their full contexts. The alleged initial sense and semantic links among opposition, wrongness, and negation remain uncertain.

The 不 + 惟 fusion is a disputed proposal about spoken lexical history. Neither the evidence inspected here nor the proposal demonstrates graphical composition from 不 and 惟. The reconstruction of 非 alone cannot establish a depicted object’s name or a sound borrowing based on that name.

The search did not retrieve a verified query-specific Xiaoxuetang 非 record page or direct image URL. The candidate image is a modern vector redraw attributed by its Commons description to Xiaoxuetang record 45.EC02; it is not an artifact photograph. No other glyph candidate with independently checked provenance and reuse terms was selected.

No direct primary reconstruction list was successfully inspected in this invocation; the pronunciation comparison is limited to the inspected scholarly discussion. No phonetic component in 非’s own graph is proposed, so component-level sound-role claims are not made.

The direct SVG could not be fetched as an image by the browser tool, and the linked Xiaoxuetang record page failed to load. The candidate is retained because the opened Commons description identifies the exact Xiaoxuetang record, source corpus references, and CC0/public-domain status; no visual inspection is claimed.

The available image is a modern Inkscape redraw in Shang oracle-script style, not an ancient artifact photograph. The Commons description associates it with 甲骨文編799 / 合集34479; the exact underlying database image was not separately retrieved.
